description: Sabotages of durable-ioring-events that only a trace session can catch: tests/session.rs, run with --include-ignored. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1 from an elevated process or one in the Performance Log Users group, as CI's runners are (DE-D-4); unelevated, every session test fails to start and the baseline is red, so the sweep stops before any entry.
notCoveredHere: What a unit test can see is sabotage.json.

sabotages.name: DE-D-6: a pair's begin is written in an activity no end will share
sabotages.why: The begin's activity is the one its end looks up; one created and not held leaves the end to create another, and the pair is two activities.

sabotages.name: DE-D-6: a pair's end is written in an activity of its own
sabotages.why: The end must repeat its begin's activity, or a reader cannot pair them by it.

sabotages.name: DE-D-6: a pair's events are written in the thread's activity
sabotages.why: Written by the plain call, a begin and an end on two threads carry the two threads' ids, and a pair whose end comes from another thread is never one activity.

sabotages.name: DE-D-6: an end whose begin was not written is written in the thread's activity
sabotages.why: An end with no begin written is an activity of its own, so that it joins no other.

sabotages.name: DE-D-6 control: no activity is spelled another way for an event that is not a pair
sabotages.why: A control: the same value by another spelling, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: DE-D-7: an end lets its pair go only when it is written
sabotages.why: An end reported after its session stopped is not written and must still release what was held for its pair, or the process map grows by a pair for each stop. A later session then writes an end of that pair in the begin's activity, which `a_pair_ended_through_a_fan_out_after_its_session_stopped_is_let_go` reads.
